title: Marks
statementMd:
There is a circular track with b𝑏 equally spaced positions, numbered 0,1,…,b−10,1,…,𝑏−1 clockwise. Adjacent positions are 11 unit apart, so the whole circle measures b𝑏 units.

A marker starts at position 00 and, at every step, advances by a fixed a𝑎 positions clockwise (wrapping back to 00 after position b−1𝑏−1). It successively stops at pk=(a⋅k)modb,k=0,1,…,n−1,

𝑝𝑘=(𝑎⋅𝑘)mod𝑏,𝑘=0,1,…,𝑛−1,

leaving a mark at each stop, for a total of n𝑛 marks. It is guaranteed that gcd(a,b)=1gcd(𝑎,𝑏)=1∗∗ and n≤b𝑛≤𝑏, so these n𝑛 marks are pairwise distinct.

These n𝑛 marks divide the circle into n𝑛 arcs. The length of an arc is the number of units it spans (every arc length is a positive integer, and the lengths sum to b𝑏).

How many **distinct** arc-length values are there? For each value, what is it, and how many times does it occur?

∗∗gcd(a,b)=cgcd(𝑎,𝑏)=𝑐 means that c𝑐 is the largest positive integer such that c𝑐 divides both a𝑎 and b𝑏.

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t𝑡. The description of the test cases follows.

The only line of each test case contains three integers a𝑎, b𝑏, and n𝑛, representing the parameters of this test case.

- 1≤t≤301≤𝑡≤30
- 1≤a<b≤10181≤𝑎<𝑏≤1018
- gcd(a,b)=1gcd(𝑎,𝑏)=1
- 2≤n≤b2≤𝑛≤𝑏

## Output

For each test case, first output the number of distinct arc-length values, d𝑑.

Followed by d𝑑 lines, output 22 integers s𝑠 and c𝑐 for each of which, representing that exactly c𝑐 arcs have length s𝑠.

For each test case, output these lines **in increasing order of s𝑠**.

## Note

**Explanation for Sample 1**

The marks are {0,7,2,9,4,11,6}{0,7,2,9,4,11,6}, which, when sorted, are 0,2,4,6,7,9,110,2,4,6,7,9,11. The consecutive arc lengths are 2,2,2,1,2,2,12,2,2,1,2,2,1, so length 11 occurs 22 times and length 22 occurs 55 times.
